newsitem.title: UK: LPC - Banks vie for major UK power plant financings.
newsitem.headline: LPC - Banks vie for major UK power plant financings.

text.p: LONDON, Sept 12 (LPC) - A host of international banks are competing to finance up to 1.6 billion sterling ($2.49 billion) in debt for British power plant projects, according to banking sources. The massive Teeside Power and Humber Power companies are currently negotiating with potential lenders to refinance existing debt and for fresh funds for expansion.

Humber Power Ltd is seeking about 275 million stg for construction of the 510-megawatt second phase of its power station in Humberside, bankers say. Humber Power may also refinance the 520 million stg credit that financed its 750- megawatt first phase.

A number of banks - including ABN AMRO Bank, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, Deutsche Bank, HSBC, NatWest Markets and Union Bank of Switzerland - are making proposals to Humber Power, which is sponsored by Imatran Voima Oy, Midlands Electricity and ABB-Asea Brown Boveri.
Humber's first phase, not due to come on stream until 1997, is financed via a 17.5-year loan struck in 1994. The bulk of that credit is priced 110 bps over LIBOR.
At the same time, Teeside Power Ltd is in talks with banks for a refinancing of the 795 million stg project financing of its plant in Cleveland, according to bank sources.

Teeside, which is controlled by Enron Corp unit Enron Power, is currently taking bids from at least three banks. Teeside is already in operation and will seek a loan of at least 12 years. Pricing on its current deal, put into place in 1991, ranges between 87.5 bps and 137.5 bps over LIBOR.
